title: The Easiest Online Business to Start in 2026
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: Most examples are reverse-engineered claims rather than operator interviews. The host promotes a HighLevel signup link and his own Playmakers community, which may influence the examples and recommendations.

idea.name: GoHighLevel / HighLevel
idea.one_liner: A CRM and business software platform that agencies use to build and white-label niche software products.
idea.customer: Agencies and entrepreneurs building software for businesses.
idea.offer: CRM, websites, funnels, courses, memberships, email and a platform for white-label software.
idea.revenue_model: Recurring SaaS subscription; the platform is also used by customers to sell their own subscriptions.

key_quotes.quote: In this case, it's high level.

claims.claim: The host says every business on his list has over 1,000 paying customers and almost all charge $50 to $5,000 a month.
claims.quote: every business on this list has over 1,000 paying customers and almost every one of them charges between $50 and $5,000 a month.

claims.claim: The host estimates the listed white-label businesses could generate from $50,000 to over $1 million per month.
claims.quote: You do the math, from 50 grand a month to over a million dollars a month, all built on top of someone else's software.

claims.claim: The host says HighLevel has more than 70,000 agencies as potential customers for add-ons.
claims.quote: So their customers are the 70 plus thousand high level agencies, including a lot of the people watching this video right now.

claims.claim: The host says HighLevel costs $300 to $500 a month as a platform for building a business.
claims.quote: Every single company we just covered pays high level the same cost, somewhere between $300 and $500 a month, flat, forever.

claims.claim: The host says the platform bill stays the same whether the customer has 10 or 10,000 customers.
claims.quote: Doesn't matter if they have 10 customers or 10,000 customers, that bill never goes away.

claims.claim: The host says using HighLevel as one's own CRM costs $97 a month.
claims.quote: And remember, if you use high level as your own CRM and you're not white labeling it and selling it to others, it's 97 a month, okay?

claims.claim: The host says the platform tier costs $300 to $500 a month.
claims.quote: It's only 300 to 500 a month if you're using it as a platform to build an entire business on.

claims.claim: The host says his signup link usually gives 14 days free and offers 30 days free in this instance.
claims.quote: It's usually 14 days free with my link.

claims.claim: The host says his signup link gives 30 days free.
claims.quote: You get 30 days free just to poke around with all the features that they offer.

ideas.delivery: HighLevel supplies the software platform online; customers configure it and sell branded versions to their own audiences.
ideas.other_uk_rules: CRM data processing falls under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Recurring subscription plans may fall under DMCC Act subscription-contract rules.

idea.name: Loan Signing System
idea.one_liner: A course and white-labeled CRM for mobile notaries, sold on a monthly or annual subscription.
idea.customer: Mobile notaries and people who notarize documents.
idea.offer: Notary training plus CRM software for tracking customers, work and emails.
idea.revenue_model: Course sales and recurring monthly or annual software subscriptions.

key_quotes.quote: So if you are a mobile notary, you would pay him 100 bucks a month to have a CRM, a customer relationship management platform.

claims.claim: The host says the business makes over $100,000 a month.
claims.quote: Guys, there's a guy out here selling notary software, notary software, the most boring thing I can think of, and he's making over $100,000 a month, and he didn't even build the software.

claims.claim: The host says the business makes millions of dollars a year.
claims.quote: Millions of dollars a year, selling software to people who notarized documents in their cars.

claims.claim: The host says the course costs about $400.
claims.quote: So this website is where he sells like a $400 course, which is great.

claims.claim: The host says the software costs $97 a month or $1,000 a year.
claims.quote: It's 97 bucks a month or 1000 bucks a year.

claims.claim: The host says the business has over 1,000 customers.
claims.quote: And remember, he is a diamond level high level award winner, which means he has over 1000 customers that is proven and verified.

claims.claim: The host estimates the business makes at least $100,000 a month.
claims.quote: So at a bare minimum, he's doing 100,000 a month and I hope that it's way more.

claims.claim: The host says a mobile notary would pay about $100 a month for the CRM.
claims.quote: So if you are a mobile notary, you would pay him 100 bucks a month to have a CRM, a customer relationship management platform.

claims.claim: The host recommends partnering with micro-influencers who have 5,000 or 50,000 followers.
claims.quote: You can use someone else's audience, micro influencers with 5,000, 50,000 followers

claims.claim: The host suggests splitting the partnership proceeds 50/50.
claims.quote: build this for them, split it with them 50, 50

acquisition_channels.details: The host recommends pitching micro-influencers through Twitter, Strava and Facebook DMs, and sending a message through PayPal. These are proposed tactics, not verified channels used by the company.

ideas.delivery: The business sells an online course and provides a white-labeled CRM subscription to notaries.

uk_legal_risk.reason: The recommended partner-acquisition tactic uses unsolicited social DMs to individual micro-influencers, who may be consumers or sole traders; the transcript also suggests repeated unsolicited PayPal messages.

ideas.other_uk_rules: CRM data processing falls under UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Recurring subscriptions may fall under DMCC Act subscription-contract rules.

idea.name: PushPress
idea.one_liner: Gym check-in software that expands into CRM and gym management subscriptions.
idea.offer: Check-in software, CRM and additional gym-management features.
idea.revenue_model: Monthly software subscriptions, setup fees and upsells.

key_quotes.quote: They started as simply check-in software for gyms.

claims.claim: The host says one plan costs $229 a month plus a $700 setup fee.
claims.quote: 229 bucks a month plus a $700 set of fee and I dug a little deeper.

claims.claim: The host says other plans cost $550 to $600 a month.
claims.quote: It's not shown on this page, but they have other plans that bump you up to 550 to 600 bucks a month.

claims.claim: The host says PushPress has at least 1,000 customers.
claims.quote: Remember, they have at least a thousand customers minimum.

claims.claim: The host assumes an average customer pays $200 a month.
claims.quote: So we'll take an average and say the average customers pay in 200 a month.

claims.claim: Using that assumed average, the host calculates over $200,000 a month and millions per year.
claims.quote: That's over $200,000 a month, millions of dollars a year with almost no cost from one product line.

claims.claim: The host estimates revenue is well over $5 million a year.
claims.quote: Then you got set up fees, upsells, and I bet you anything they're doing well over a 5 million bucks a year.
